title: EVA 2027 - HEC Montréal
text:
Welcome on the home page of Extreme Value Analysis 2027 (EVA 2027). EVA is a biennial international conference on extreme value analysis, probabilistic and statistical models and their applications.
The 15th edition will be hosted by HEC Montréal in downtown Montréal (Québec, Canada) at the Hélène-Desmarais building from Monday July 5th until Friday July 9th, 2027. Satellite courses will take place on Saturday and Sunday, July 3rd to 4th.

title: EVA 2027 - HEC Montréal
text:
The data challenge for the Extreme Value Analysis 2027 conference is organized in collaboration with the International Air Transport Association (IATA), headquartered in Montréal. It consists of three prediction tasks related to the estimation of the extremal characteristics of in-flight turbulence events experienced by transatlantic flights.
Registration will open soon!



Participating teams must register via the Microsoft form (the link can be found at the end of the PDF containing the description of the challenge and the instructions) before January 31st, 2027. The maximum team size is 10.
Upon registering via the form, all participating team members will have to sign an electronic non-disclosure agreement (NDA) with IATA, who own the rights to the data, in order to participate in the challenge.
After all participants have e-signed the NDA, the challenge organisers will share the dataset via email with the corresponding team member.
Teams will be invited to submit preliminary predictions before May 1st, 2027 by sending the four parquet files in a ZIP file by email to Jordan Richards. All teams who submitted will then receive a preliminary ranking, for both the individual tasks and the overall aggregated score.
The final deadline for submission is June 1st, 2027. As part of the final submission, we ask that the participants provide a brief summary of the methodology used for tackling each of the three tasks as a bullet point list with potentially scientific references, if available.

The contact person for the data challenge is Jordan Richards (University of Edinburgh)

title: Hotels
text:
Travel and visa
You may need an electronic travel authorization (eTA) or a visitor visa. Check this video for more details about the application. Please contact the organizing committee if you need a letter for your visa application.
Montréal-Trudeau International Airport (YUL) is well connected with major American and European cities. The airport is easily reached via the 747 bus.

title: Hotels
text:
Accommodation
Please note that Montreal International Jazz Festival runs from June 25th until July 4th. We encourage you to secure your accommodation well in advance, particularly if you plan to attend the short courses over the weekend.
The organizing committee will contact hotels to book rooms at a discounted rate. There are numerous hostels, hotels and bed and breakfasts close to downtown.

title: Previous editions
text:
The inception of EVA dates back to Vimeiro meeting in Portugal in 1983 in August 31st–September 14th. Further meetings in the field were organized in Oberwolfach with the 1987 Conference on Extremewertheorie, and the Gaithersburg 1993 Conference on Extreme Value Theory and its Applications.
Previous editions of EVA took place in:

Göteborg, Sweden (1998)
Leuven, Belgium (2001)
Aveiro, Portugal (2004)
Göteborg, Sweden (2005)
Bern, Switzerland (2007)
Fort Collins, Colorado, USA (2009)
Lyon, France (2011)
Shanghai, China (2013)
Ann Arbor, Michigan, USA (2015)
Delft, Netherlands (2017)
Zagreb, Croatia (2019)
Edinburgh, UK (2021, virtual)
Milano, Italy (2023)
Chapel Hill, North Carolina, USA (2025)

title: Venue
text:
The conference and satellite courses will take place in the Hélène-Desmarais building in downtown Montréal. Consult the website for a map of the floors (3rd floor and 4th floor)
The address of the venue is 501, rue de la Gauchetière Ouest, Montréal, H2Z 1Z5.






The downtown campus is easily reached by public transport, either via metro (Square-Victoria-OACI station, orange line), or from the Gare Centrale REM station.
The coffee breaks and standing lunches will take place in the A.373 Centre de conférence Claude-Séguin, located next to the Entrée Famille Karim (boul. René-Lévesque Ouest).
Plenary talks will take place in room A.335 Amphithéâtre Rachelle et Alain-Paris.
Registration will be at room A.393.
Contributed and invited talks will be in classrooms

C.403 Louis-R.-Chênevert
C.409 Gilles-Labbé
C.415 Pierre Fitzgibbon
C.406 Josée-Fiset
C.412 Malette

title: EVA 2027 - HEC Montréal
text:
The tasks of the scientific committee all relate to the organization of the scientific activities. The scientific committee will:

oversee invited talks (determining topics and organizers),
review the contributed talks proposals, build the program and make a schedule,
organize the satellite workshops and short courses
prepare and oversee the data challenge, including the special issue for Extremes
organize a poster competition and judge the latter
determine, together with members of the Extremes board, the best paper award for junior researchers.

The committee for the 2027 edition of EVA is formed of:

Boris Béranger (University of New South Wales Sidney)
Miguel de Carvalho (University of Edinburgh), communication officer
Clément Dombry (Université de Franche-Comté)
Anna Kiriliouk (Université catholique de Louvain)
Thomas Mikosch (University of Copenhagen)
Philippe Naveau (LSCE, CNRS)
Thomas Opitz (INRAE Avignon)
Jordan Richards (University of Edinburgh), data challenge organizer
Anne Sabourin (Université Paris Cité), chairperson
Johan Segers (KU Leuven)
Emma Simpson (University College London)
Benjamin Shaby (Colorado State University)
Stilian Stoev (University of Michigan)
Kirstin Strokorb (University of Bath)
Gilles Stupfler (Université d’Angers)
Thordis Thorarinsdottir (University of Oslo)
